lines: I remember your hand steadying the bottle while I tried to drink.
You kept talking until I could understand words again.
The room stopped spinning when I heard you say my name.
I woke with no sense of direction, and you stayed until it returned.
I lost every road for a while. You <pulse>marked the way back</pulse>.
My first clear memory is your face beside the bed.
I remember the cure tasting awful and your voice telling me to finish it.
You did not leave when I was frightened of everyone in the room.
The village looked unfamiliar at first. You walked it with me anyway.
I can hold a compass again because you refused to give up on me.
You gave me time to remember where home was.
I still have gaps in that night, but your kindness is not one of them.
The first map I opened afterward made sense. I nearly cried over it.
I remember sunlight on the table and you waiting for me to speak.
You answered the same confused question until I finally believed you.
I was lost inside my own head. You helped me find the edge of it.
The cure saved me, but somebody still had to bring it. That was you.
I know what it cost to stay through the worst of it. Thank you.
You saw me when I was barely myself and treated me like I would return.
I am here, working, and able to remember why. I owe you for that.
I know I have seen you before, but I cannot place the room.
Were you holding a bottle, or am I borrowing that from a dream?
Your voice feels familiar even when the memory does not.
I remember a table above me and someone saying the fever had broken.
There was a compass near the bed. Did you put it there?
I keep seeing your face through a haze of green glass.
The way back is missing pieces. You seem to be in several of them.
I know you helped me. I wish I knew exactly how.
Did I ask you where I was more than once?
I remember reaching for a map and being unable to read it.
Someone opened the window after I woke. Was that you?
The cure comes back as a taste before it comes back as a memory.
I thought the ceiling was moving. You may have been the one who calmed me.
Your name is clearer than the rest of that day.
I remember footsteps leaving and returning. I think they were yours.
Was I afraid of the compass, or only the needle moving?
I can trace the day up to the cure, then everything blurs.
People tell me you stayed nearby. That sounds right when I look at you.
I am still fitting the memory together. Please do not rush me.
Whatever happened in that room, I came out alive and you were there.
I know you brought the cure. Please stay on the other side of the table.
I am grateful, but being near you still pulls me back into that room.
Tell me before you move closer. Sudden steps are difficult right now.
You helped me survive. That does not make the memory gentle.
I need the door clear while we talk.
Please keep your hands where I can see them.
Some of what I remember is fear, and your face is tangled in it.
I believe you meant to help. My body has not learned that yet.
Do not ask me to recount the cure today.
I can thank you from here. Let that be enough for now.
The smell of potions still turns my stomach.
I woke surrounded by strangers, and you were the closest one.
Give me time to separate what happened from who saved me.
I am trying not to mistake memory for danger.
Please do not touch my shoulder without asking.
I know the cure worked. I also know I still wake frightened.
Your kindness is real. So is the panic that comes with remembering it.
We can speak, but I may need to stop without explaining why.
I want to trust this conversation. Distance will help.
Thank you for bringing me back. Now let me choose how close you stand.
